title: Uniform open direct-image vanishing from the base-field torsion bound
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $c\ge0$ be an integer with $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)\le c$ [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion with $X$ separated of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $d=\dim U$ if $U\ne\varnothing$ and $d=0$ otherwise, with topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $A$ be any finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. On the small etale sites, for every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules and integer $q>2d+c$,
$$R^qj_*M=0.$$
Here $Rj_*$ is the ordinary module-sheaf derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The integer bound depends only on $U,k,c$, and works for all such $A$, hence for all $A_{E,n}$ at once. More explicitly, every affine etale $V\to X$ has $V\times_XU$ finite type over $k$ of dimension at most $d$, and its etale torsion cohomology with every $\ell$-primary coefficient sheaf vanishes in degrees $>2d+c$. The higher module direct-image sheaves agree with the corresponding higher abelian direct-image sheaves after forgetting the coefficient action. If $U=\varnothing$ all these cohomology and direct-image objects are zero. No separable-closedness hypothesis on $k$ is imposed.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian. The open immersion j is quasi-compact over a locally Noetherian target, so j followed by the structure morphism is finite type. Apply lem-kun-dimension-finite-type and the elementary WithBot/ENat conversion to obtain dim U <= d = ((dim U).unbotD 0).toNat, with equality when U is nonempty.

For affine etale V over X, compactness of V and quasi-separatedness of X give quasi-compactness of V -> X. Base change and composition give finite type of W = V x_X U over k. Its projection to U is etale. Use the already proved source theorem Scheme.Hom.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_etale: discrete fibres imply that distinct specializing points have distinct images, so strict specialization chains map to strict chains. Thus dim W <= dim U <= d; no local-ring dimension calculation is needed.

For nonempty W its dimension is a natural number e <= d. The finite-type torsion cohomological bound gives cd_tor(W) <= 2e+c <= 2d+c. For empty W every sheaf is zero by the empty etale covering, hence every cohomology group is zero. This proves cd_tor(W) <= 2d+c uniformly. A primary torsion module sheaf has torsion geometric stalks since powers of the prime are positive; the stalkwise characterization of torsion makes its underlying abelian sheaf locally torsion. A requested integer degree q is positive and equals the cast of q.toNat, so the bound gives the affine-test cohomology clause.

Every module over the finite ring A is torsion as an additive group. Apply the source finite-ring torsion lemma on geometric stalks and isTorsionModuleSheaf_iff_isTorsion. Apply lem-sfb-higher-direct-image-affine-etale-bound to the underlying abelian sheaf with the test bound of the preceding step. This theorem supplies the sheafification and affine-cover argument and gives zero abelian higher direct image above 2d+c.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison to M[0]. Compose its degree-q homology isomorphism with the exact-forgetting homology and single-complex isomorphisms. This is the requested coefficient comparison. Faithfulness of forgetting reflects a zero identity, so the zero abelian higher direct image implies zero module higher direct image.

If U is empty the empty covering forces every module or abelian sheaf on U to be zero. Additive single, derived direct-image, cohomology and homology functors preserve zero objects, in every integer degree. For each test pullback its projection to U makes it empty, so its cohomology is zero as well. The bound only uses U and c; neither finite ring A nor its specified prime-power annihilator changes it.
